Even if you use a computer software program, there's no substitute for the assistance of an experienced tax professional.

questions.q: Do you handle business and individual taxes?
questions.a: Yes, we handle both individual and business taxes, ranging from straightforward 1040 filings to complex multi-entity tax structures. Whether you're a W-2 employee, a self-employed freelancer, or a business owner with multiple entities, we have the expertise to navigate your tax situation efficiently and strategically.

questions.q: What information and documents do you need from me to get started?
questions.a: During our initial consultation, our Director of Practice Management will review your specific tax needs and outline the required documentation. To begin the process, we'll request that you upload relevant financial records, prior-year tax returns, and any supporting documents into our secure client portal. Then we will assess your situation, provide a detailed quote, and send out an engagement letter.

questions.q: Can you assist with business structuring and tax efficiency strategies?
questions.a: Yes, we frequently work with clients on business structuring and tax efficiency planning. Whether you're launching a new business, restructuring an existing one, or considering entity changes (LLC, S-Corp, C-Corp, etc.), we analyze your financial goals and tax implications to recommend the most advantageous structure.

services.title: Tax Planning
services.summary: Strategies put in place before year-end.
services.text: Effective tax planning happens before it is time to file. We evaluate your projected tax liability, identify planning opportunities and develop strategies that can be implemented before year-end.
services.lead: Work with an experienced Houston CPA team to evaluate your projected tax liability, identify planning opportunities, and implement proactive strategies before year-end. Whether you need a tax projection, a focused consultation, or a more comprehensive business tax plan, our team can provide the level of guidance that fits your situation.

covers.title: 2-Minute Drill Consultation
covers.text: A one-hour meeting reviewing your previously filed return to determine any life or business changes and relevant tax law changes, and you leave with a planning cheat sheet of tax questions for the future.

covers.title: Tax Projection
covers.text: A brief phone call about yearly changes and expectations, a projection based on last year's numbers and current activity, then a one-hour meeting to discuss it and answer questions.

covers.title: Individual or Business Tax Plan
covers.text: An initial meeting with a tax preparer, a full financial model run on your adjusted numbers, a year-end action list to help mitigate exposure, and a summary meeting where findings are discussed to set a direction.

covers.title: Multiple scenarios
covers.text: We develop multiple scenarios so you can visualize the effect of the various strategies we are proposing, then meet to discuss the plan.

questions.q: What is a tax plan?
questions.a: A Tax Plan provides peace of mind and an opportunity to minimize your tax liability. It consists of reviewing business and personal financial documents used to compute estimated tax liability. The Plan provides insightful information that allows you to make business decisions that create additional tax deductions or the deferral of revenues to reduce your tax liability. It is critical to act on the strategies selected before year end because after December 31 it is merely history.

questions.q: What's the difference between tax preparation and tax planning?
questions.a: Tax preparation focuses primarily on reporting activity that has already occurred and preparing the required returns. Tax planning is forward-looking and evaluates potential strategies and decisions before year-end so there is still time to act.

questions.q: Is getting a tax plan only beneficial for businesses or is it beneficial for individuals as well?
questions.a: A Tax Plan is very beneficial for individuals who have complex tax returns. If you have a sole proprietorship it is basically reporting business activity in your personal tax filing that has the same complexities as an actual business tax return filing. You have harvesting of losses, non-cash deductions, rental properties, passive activity income from K-1s, and the tax attributes of other personal investments that create the need for a plan.

questions.q: How would you reduce my taxes?
questions.a: By preparing a plan and gathering your financial documents we can clearly see your business and personal activity. We look for methods to accelerate expenses, defer income, or identify investment opportunities that will allow for minimizing your taxes. This process will be completed before year-end to allow for the implementation of the identified strategies.

questions.q: What are the steps for a tax plan?
questions.a: Set up an appointment to discuss your business and personal activity. Gather your documents and update your financial accounting records with the most current information. Accounting clean-up may be necessary to have solid financial information to create the plan. After creating the projection and reviewing your financial records we may request additional documentation to reduce your projected liability. We will have a meeting once the plan is completed to discuss the strategies being recommended. You will need to execute the strategies.

questions.q: What industries or types of businesses do you specialize in?

Our team is equipped to handle diverse business types and unique situations. During our Meet & Greet we take the time to understand your specific needs and tailor our services accordingly.

questions.q: What is a Fractional CFO?
questions.a: A Fractional CFO provides ongoing financial leadership without joining the company as a full-time internal executive. The scope can include reporting, forecasting, cash-flow planning, budgeting, performance analysis and strategic financial guidance.

questions.q: What size company is the service designed for?
questions.a: The service is designed primarily for owner-led companies beginning at approximately $5 million in annual revenue. The appropriate level depends on company size, complexity, entity count, transaction volume and strategic needs.

questions.q: Is bookkeeping included?

questions.q: Can Cooper CPA Group help prepare my business for a sale?
questions.a: The higher service levels include support for value creation, exit readiness, financial diligence preparation, valuation and ownership-transition planning.

questions.q: Are tax services included?
questions.a: Tax planning and business and personal tax returns are included within the service framework. The exact scope is confirmed in the engagement proposal.

questions.q: Is this an audit or review engagement?
questions.a: No. Fractional CFO services are advisory and accounting services and are not an audit, review or attestation engagement.

services.title: Quality of Earnings
services.summary: QoE reports scoped to the size of the deal.
services.text: From smaller acquisitions to complex, multi-entity transactions, our Quality of Earnings engagements are scoped around the size and complexity of the deal, with fixed fees confirmed before work begins.
services.lead: We analyze historical earnings and financial trends to provide a clearer picture of the business's underlying financial performance, and evaluate EBITDA adjustments and add-backs to help distinguish recurring earnings from owner-related, nonrecurring or unusual items.

covers.title: Standard, starting at $12,500
covers.text: Generally suited for a single-entity acquisition with a purchase price of approximately $5 million or less and records in a single accounting system. Proof of cash analysis, adjusted EBITDA with supporting documentation, review of owner compensation, related-party transactions and customer concentration. Approximately 3 to 4 weeks.

covers.title: Core, starting at $22,500
covers.text: Generally suited for transactions involving one to three entities and purchase prices of approximately $5 million to $10 million. Standard-level procedures plus month-by-month earnings analysis, working capital trends, debt-like item schedules, receivables and payables aging with DSO and DPO, and a source-linked Excel databook with a key findings summary. Approximately 4 to 5 weeks.

covers.title: Comprehensive, varies by scope
covers.text: Designed for larger or more complex transactions where deal size, entity structure, financial complexity or requested support requires a more tailored scope of work.

covers.title: Scoping and proposal
covers.text: We discuss the transaction, financing requirements, entity structure, timeline and expected scope, review the available financial records, data room and accounting system access, then provide a defined scope, estimated timeline, deliverables and engagement fee. Starting prices are estimates; final scope, deliverables, timeline and fees are confirmed in the engagement letter.

covers.title: Scoped separately
covers.text: Working capital peg and purchase agreement support, tax diligence and exposure review, transaction structure and tax modeling, forward projections and pro forma modeling, additional entities beyond the agreed scope, sell-side or vendor Quality of Earnings, and accelerated delivery subject to availability.

questions.q: What is a Quality of Earnings report?
questions.a: A Quality of Earnings report analyzes a company's financial performance to help determine how much of its reported earnings are accurate, recurring and sustainable. It can also identify adjustments, unusual expenses and potential financial risks.

questions.q: What will a QofE review?
questions.a: The required analysis may include historical and trailing 12-month cash activity, reported earnings, add-backs and adjustments, customer concentration, contract continuity, and the sustainability of revenue and margins.

questions.q: Who prepares the required QoE?
questions.a: The required QoE must be completed by an independent financial professional for the benefit of the lender, rather than by the buyer or seller.

questions.q: How could a QoE affect SBA financing?
questions.a: Lenders will use the earnings determined through the QoE when evaluating qualifying transactions. If normalized earnings differ from the figures originally presented, it could affect debt service coverage, financing structure or other aspects of the deal.

questions.q: Can a buyer or seller order the required SBA QoE?
questions.a: Under the new SBA requirements, the required QoE must be performed by an independent, experienced financial professional for the lender's benefit. A report prepared by or for the borrower or seller cannot satisfy that requirement. Buyers should coordinate with their lender regarding the specific requirements for their transaction.

services.title: Succession Planning
services.summary: Planning a family or third-party transition.
services.text: For small and mid-market business owners, retirement is a transition that affects leadership, ownership, cash flow and family dynamics. We help you design a plan that protects the long-term future of the business.
services.lead: Retirement isn't just walking away. More than seven out of ten small or mid-market businesses fail to survive the transition from founder to second generation, typically falling prey to lack of innovation, poor management or estate taxes, or family discord. A well-designed succession plan is essential to protecting the long-term future of your business.
services.imageAlt: An older business owner talking through plans across a desk

covers.title: Business valuation

covers.title: Business restructuring
covers.text: We evaluate whether entity restructuring, shareholder agreements or recapitalization are necessary to facilitate a smooth transition while protecting control and flexibility.

covers.title: Tax consequences
covers.text: We analyze potential income, gift and estate tax exposure and develop strategies to minimize the overall burden while maintaining compliance.

covers.title: Retirement projections
covers.text: Detailed retirement cash flow projections to determine whether the transition strategy supports your lifestyle goals and long-term financial independence.

covers.title: Tax projections
covers.text: We model future tax scenarios under various transition structures to evaluate the long-term impact on both you and the next generation.

questions.q: What happens to the business when you are no longer running it?
questions.a: For small and mid-market business owners, retirement is not simply a decision to stop coming into the office. It is a transition that affects leadership, ownership, cash flow and family dynamics, and conversations around aging, legacy and financial affairs are easier to have early than late.

questions.q: Will the transition generate enough income to support your retirement goals?
questions.a: We prepare detailed retirement cash flow projections to determine whether the transition strategy supports your lifestyle goals and long-term financial independence.

questions.q: Family transfer or third-party sale?
questions.a: We evaluate your options and help you choose the right path, then clearly structure who will lead and who will own.

questions.q: Who will lead and who will own?
questions.a: We clearly structure management and ownership transitions, and evaluate whether entity restructuring, shareholder agreements or recapitalization are needed to make the transfer work.

questions.q: How can taxes be minimized?
questions.a: We design strategies to reduce tax exposure and preserve value, analyzing potential income, gift and estate tax exposure and modelling future tax scenarios under various transition structures.

questions.q: How do we keep it fair when family is involved?
questions.a: Relationships, expectations, and long-standing dynamics often influence decisions in ways that financial models alone cannot solve. We help align expectations and reduce family tension.

facts.heading: What the year brought
items: 2023: launched consulting packages for start-ups and established businesses, expanded buy-side consulting and due diligence, and strengthened internal training

2024: welcomed client care specialists, enhanced technology tools for bookkeeping and reporting, expanded advisory beyond tax preparation into ongoing financial strategy, and deepened community involvement

2025: upgraded internal systems and automations, introduced the Quarterly Close Process, expanded industry partnerships in valuations, banking and legal services, and rolled out advanced tax planning strategies
2026: expanded proactive tax planning, strengthened bookkeeping and advisory support, continued improving internal systems, and grew industry partnerships
